content: Cefdinir is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. To achieve the best results, it is important to take this medication at evenly spaced intervals and to complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Certain medications may bind to cefdinir, reducing its absorption. Common side effects of cefdinir include diarrhea, headache, and nausea. This medication may also cause stools to appear reddish in color, particularly if taken alongside iron supplements. This discoloration is harmless. It is important to note that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, cefdinir may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea. This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of cefdinir may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection, which are fungal infections. Severe allergic reactions to cefdinir are rare but can occur. Symptoms of a serious allergic reaction may include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. Before taking cefdinir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin). Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefdinir may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as determined by your doctor. Cefdinir does not pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefdinir may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false test results. If someone overdoses on cefdinir and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other infections unless directed by your doctor. While taking cefdinir, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as kidney function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Be sure to attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose of cefdinir, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store cefdinir at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about cefdinir. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
